name: Example: Calculating a Derivative Using Multiple Instances of the Chain Rule
worked_solution:
First, we express $y$ as a composite function

$$
y = u^4, \qquad u = \cos{v}, \qquad v = 2x.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\dfrac{\textrm d y}{\textrm d u} = 4u^3,\qquad \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm d v} = -\sin{v},\qquad \dfrac{\textrm{d}v}{\textrm d x} = 2.
$$

Applying now the chain rule twice, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}v}\cdot \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} \\  & =4{u}^{3}\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡v)\cdot (2) \\  & =4(\operatorname{cos}⁡2x)^{3}\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡2x)\cdot (2) \\  & =-8{cos}^{3}⁡2x\operatorname{sin}⁡2x.\end{aligned}
$$
